statement: What value of $x$ satisfies the equation $\sqrt[3]{2x + 1} = 3$?

choices.misconception: I did not undo the cube root at all and solved $2x + 1 = 3$, which gives $x = 1$.
I squared both sides as if it were a square root, so I solved $2x + 1 = 9$ and got $x = 4$.
I cubed correctly to get $2x + 1 = 27$, but then added $1$ instead of subtracting it, so $2x = 28$ and $x = 14$.

hints: To undo a cube root, raise both sides to the third power.
Cube both sides, then solve the linear equation.

solutions.reliable: Cubing both sides gives $2x + 1 = 27$, so $2x = 26$ and $x = 13$. Check: $\sqrt[3]{2(13) + 1} = \sqrt[3]{27} = 3$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
